purpose: Make the actual R24 G4 torque controller and causal post-release contact detector work together. Compare complete physically simulated systems, not sums of separate papers. Never change R10 or the original.
incumbent: r24 support-deadband controller plus its actual R14 coupled detector, and R10/R19 as secondary control floors
primary_known_input: R24 landing late force cohorts (4 matched +/-X or +/-Z forces; three old normal controls and three additional previously disclosed normals).
first_hypotheses: same controller plus entire unmodified R25 detector
coupled base plus actual detach-only horizontal R23 sensor
coupled plus signed 3-D unloaded reaction using normal-only bound and physical ownership
normal_bound: First assess whole detached force vector. Frozen signed vertical excursions relative to zero under all fit normals; use each signed normal maximum * 1.2 + 0.5 N (and symmetric R23 horizontal threshold). Must exceed all audit normals without retuning. If absolute z never separates the positives, compare physics-motivated common-mode/short horizon normal calibration as a separate registered attempt, not adjudicating it with the same blind panel.
qualifying: Unchanged G4 (all four relative to R10 wherever R24 passes), no new cost/saturation/tool failure, identical controller trajectory vs R24 original for same case, no added false or extra duplicate, no old strict alarm lost or >5ms later or >5 active samples longer. Need a strict attributable gain for X and no inherited late Z regression vs both R19/R10, not merely ORing their scores.
event_contract: Same source at two close times must be separated by physical unload/reversal; no fixed clock blackout, labels, case-specific branches, actual external force, or altered inputs in detector.

separate_generalization.mechanics: fresh combos not used to choose the combined system; run only after signed detector code+parameter freeze, with same R24 and R19 comparator; do not use for retuning and still call it independent
separate_generalization.per_row: matched no-force and signed-actual-force per arm; same gates without replacing failures

scope: finite torque laboratory study, no real robot, remote, official qualification or new safety claims
